note: HCV infects no ordinary lab animal, so this class went into patients on the genotype 1b replicon for potency and rat/dog PK and toxicology for dose and safety.
label: HCV protease inhibitors

engagement.note: Simeprevir (TMC435) blocked genotype 1b replicon replication at EC50 8 nM; no patient data yet.
engagement.quote: TMC435350 inhibited HCV replication in a cellular assay (subgenomic 1b replicon) with a half-maximal effective concentration (EC(50)) of 8 nM and a selectivity index of 5,875.

engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma HCV RNA decline vs replicon RNA inhibition
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Trial NCT00938899 (TMC435350-C101) has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
engagement.note: Simeprevir 200 mg daily cut plasma HCV RNA a median 3.9 log10 in genotype 1 patients within 5 days, as the replicon predicted.
engagement.quote: Plasma HCV-RNA levels dropped rapidly in all patients, with a median maximal reduction of 3.9-log(10) IU/mL and a median of 6 days to maximal reduction.
engagement.reason: Viral load fell as replicon predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (Lin 2009 replicon, Reesink 2010 patients); viral RNA is the target's own product, so proximal tier. Replicon also predicted the genotype 3 gap, which held in patients (Moreno 2012, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2011.12.033: 'No antiviral activity was evident for genotype 3'); not entered as a separate same-status entry.

dose.model: Replicon EC99 vs rat plasma and liver exposure
dose.note: Rat plasma and liver levels 8 h after dosing exceeded the replicon EC99, the exposure target carried into first-in-human.
dose.quote: Compound concentrations detected in both plasma and liver at 8 h postdosing were above the EC(99) value measured in the replicon.

dose.magnitude_basis: once-daily plasma exposure vs replicon EC99 target
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract does not give trough-to-EC99 ratios, so whether the numeric target was met is inferred from the antiviral response.
dose.model: Replicon EC99 vs rat plasma and liver exposure
dose.note: Healthy-volunteer PK supported once-daily dosing up to 600 mg with no serious adverse events, and 200 mg daily gave potent antiviral activity in patients.
dose.quote: Once daily TMC435 given orally was generally safe and well tolerated and demonstrated potent antiviral activity.
dose.judgement: Scored same under the 'reached, drug worked' row: the regimen carried in at the rat-PK/replicon target produced the predicted response, and the drug later worked in Phase 3. Not margin_stated: the abstract states no NOAEL. Glecaprevir's review (209394 PharmR) states a 70x NOAEL margin at 300 mg, which held; not entered separately to avoid a same-status repeat. Reddy 2012 (doi:10.1128/AAC.06283-11, 14 PIs) found plasma trough/protein-shifted EC50 did not rank-order 3-day viral declines without liver-to-plasma ratios; a retrospective magnitude analysis, not scored.

efficacy.note: Replicon showed simeprevir synergistic with interferon and additive with ribavirin, the regimen later tested.
efficacy.quote: The compound was synergistic with alpha interferon and an NS5B inhibitor in the replicon model and additive with ribavirin.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: SVR12 vs replicon EC50 fold change (Q80K FC 11)
efficacy.confidence_note: Label read in full from the source bundle (sections 5.1, 12.4, 14).
efficacy.note: QUEST 1/2: SVR12 80% vs 50% on placebo; Q80K, which cut replicon potency 11-fold, cut SVR12 to 58% vs 84%.
efficacy.quote: In the OLYSIO treatment group, SVR12 rates were lower in subjects with genotype 1a virus with the NS3 Q80K polymorphism at baseline compared to subjects infected with genotype 1a virus without the Q80K polymorphism.

patient_trials.quote: An Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability Study of TMC435 in Treatment-naive, Genotype 1 Hepatitis C-infected Patients

efficacy.reason: SVR rose; Q80K loss as predicted
efficacy.judgement: comparison_stated true because the label ties the clinical Q80K loss to its microbiology section (12.4) that gives the replicon fold change. Year is the label (Nov 2013), before QUEST-1 results posted (2014-06-04). No member failed on efficacy in patients (faldaprevir stopped commercially; sovaprevir for safety), so not neg.

safety.confidence_note: Label section 13 read in full. model_first_use_year 2007 is a proxy: first-in-human trial NCT00938899 started 2007-01, so GLP toxicology preceded it.
safety.note: Simeprevir: dog heart necrosis at 28x and rat testicular findings at 0.2x human exposure; label states no patient comparison.
safety.quote: Cardiovascular toxicity consisting of acute endocardial and myocardial necrosis restricted to the left ventricular subendocardial area was seen in 2 out of 6 animals in a 2-week oral dog toxicity study

safety.magnitude_basis: AUC multiple: animal hepatobiliary toxicity at >=74x (no effect at >=3x) vs ALT >5xULN in 1% at 1x
safety.confidence_note: FDA pharmacology review (208261 PharmR) and label section 5.1 read from the source bundle.
safety.note: Grazoprevir hepatobiliary toxicity in mice and dogs (bilirubin, ALT) matched late ALT elevations in 1% of patients, rising with plasma exposure.
safety.short: Liver signal in mice, dogs, patients
safety.quote: The main target organs of toxicity identified following oral GZR administration were the liver and gallbladder (mice and dogs), with related hepatobiliary findings also observed in clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Same in kind, stated by FDA. The margin was misplaced (toxic dose >=74x in animals; ALT >5xULN in 1% of patients at clinical exposure) but the dose was not blocked, so it stays in safety rather than dose (decision 16). Hepatic decompensation in Child-Pugh B/C cirrhosis (class-wide FDA warnings) is not scored: healthy animals cannot show it.
